sentences.text:
It reveals from a perusal of the pleadings that for the purpose of upgrading of the DTP Dyke at Marwaripatty under Dibrugarh Town Mouza, a plot of land measuring 2 kathas 3 lechas covered by part of Dag No.8 of PP No.881(old)/883(old)/884(old)/885(old)/886(old)/169(new) as well as another plot of land measuring 2 kathas covered by Dag No.8 of PP No. No.881(old)/883(old)
/884(old)/885(old)/ 886(old)/169(new), both land situated at Marwaripatti under Dibrugarh Town Mouza, Assam were acquired under LA Case No.DRA 16/2013 and LA Case No.DRA 6/2018 respectively.

In respect to LA Case No.DRA 16/2013, the amount so awarded was Rs.42,60,000/-
and in respect to LA Case No.DRA 6/2018, Rs.81,31,472/- was awarded.

The petitioner claiming to be also entitled to a portion of the said awarded amount filed an application under Section 12 (1) (b)
of the Assam Land (Requisition & Acquisition) Act, 1964.
The said application having been rejected vide the order dated 17.11.2021 Page No.# 4/5 passed by the respondent No.3, the petitioner is before this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution.
3. This Court has duly perused the said application as well as the order dated 17.11.2021 passed by the respondent No.3.

It is relevant to take note of that from the materials on record, it is not clear as to whether the acquisition was made under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 or under the provisions of the Assam Land (Requisition & Acquisition) Act, 1964.

4. Be that as it may, Section 18 read with Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 or Section 12 (1) (b) of the Assam Land (Requisition & Acquisition) Act, 1964 permits a person who is entitled to compensation to file an application before the Collector requiring the matter to be referred to the Court for a decision.
5. Taking into account the above, a duty is cast upon the Collector to refer the dispute to the court for deciding as to who or how much a person would be entitled to compensation as awarded.

It is the opinion of this Court that as and when such dispute arises amongst the parties as regards the apportionment of the compensation, such dispute cannot be decided by the Collector or as has been done in the instant case by the respondent No.3 as it is the mandate of the statute that it is only the Court who can decide the same.
6.

Taking into account the above prescription of law, this Court, therefore, directs the respondent Nos.2 & 3 to refer the dispute as regards the apportionment of the compensation in respect to LA Sunil Kumar Khemani vs The State Of Assam And 8 Ors on 9 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12282168/
3 Case No. DRA 16/2013 and LA Case No.DRA 6/2016 to the Court of the competent Page No.# 5/5 jurisdiction within 15 (fifteen) days from the date of receipt of a certified copy of the instant order.

8. With the above, the instant writ petition stands disposed of.
